_comment: Mutation-testing PILOT (lg-build-verification-2639). Scoped to ONE file on purpose: this measures what a mutation gate would cost, it is not a gate. Run it with `task mutation:client`, which holds a capacity grant; nothing in lefthook.yml or CI runs it. Concurrency is NOT set here — scripts/mutation/run-client.sh sizes it from the grant, and forces jest to one worker inside each Stryker worker so the grant is not spent N times over.
_comment_jest_workers: jest.config.maxWorkers is 1 on purpose — see the jest block. run-client.sh gives the capacity grant to Stryker's concurrency, and each Stryker worker runs jest single-worker so the grant is spent once. The jest-runner also passes runInBand itself (jest-test-adapter.js), which is belt and braces rather than a reason to drop this.
_comment_ignored_test: usabilityCheckRepeatedText.test.ts is excluded from the Stryker run, and that exclusion belongs in the review list rather than in a comment nobody reads. It readFileSync's usabilityCheck.ts and asserts the source CONTAINS three regex literals and 'if (text.length < 20) continue;'. Stryker rewrites that file to instrument it, so the assertion cannot hold and the DRY RUN fails - before any mutant is tested, so no json report is written at all. A test that asserts on source text cannot be evaluated by mutation testing in principle: the operators change behaviour and the assertion reads characters. It is the TypeScript twin of server/tests/test_queue_slot_claims.py, dropped from the mutmut selection for the same reason, and both belong to the class this pilot already names - tests guarding something no operator can reach.
